aims to support 18-21-year-olds to access apprenticeships, training
and employment support. Cambridgeshire and Peterborough are one of
eight regions selected to pilot the initiative.
The pilot is being led by Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
Combined Authority (CPCA) and Peterborough City Council has been
awarded a grant through this to extend the current offer for 16-18
year olds to include young people through to the age of
21.

a deed. The grant funding will enable additional resources to be
provided to undertake the extension of the offer.

purpose:
The Government’s English
Devolution White Paper (December 2024) outlines a vision to boost
economic growth and empower communities by expanding devolution and
simplifying local councils in England. Specifically, it proposes
replacing two-tier councils with unitary authorities. In
Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, where local government is
currently split between a unitary council and a two-tier system,
all councils have been formally invited to submit reorganisation
proposals by 28 November 2025, ensuring these meet six specified
criteria (determined by MHCLG – Ministry of Housing,
Communities and local Government).  The 3 Unitary Authority – Greater
Peterborough, Mid- Cambridgeshire and Greater Cambridge – is
the LGR proposal being put forward by Peterborough Council for
consideration.

purpose:
Following consultation, a full
report on the findings and outcomes will be presented to the
council’s cabinet, who will decide whether to implement the
scheme. The Council has had a national Mandatory HMO licensing
scheme in place since 2006, however if the new scheme is
introduced, it would allow the authority to licence a much wider
range of HMOs within its area. This would include HMOs that are
occupied by three or four persons comprising two or more
households, which are currently not within the scope of Mandatory
HMO licensing. As a result, the council would have greater control
of living standards and ensure the safety of residents in its area.
Additional Licensing would also positively promote compliant
landlords and make it easier to involve all landlords in wider
strategies including crime reduction initiatives, local spatial
strategies, and other schemes. The licensing system would be
digital, making the process straightforward for applicants and also
include free guidance and training videos. The application process
would be delivered in direct partnership by The Home Safe Scheme
LTD, who are delivering the council’s Selective Licensing
scheme. The consultation also includes surveys for
residents/tenants and landlords/agents. For more information on the
consultation and to have your say visit Additional Licensing
consultation page.

entities which the council wholly owns or has a controlling

are set out in the Draft Companies Governance
Handbook.

guidance and sets out the standards and principles the council will
apply in relation to council owned entities.  It is intended to ensure that the council and

making.

has already been considered by the Shareholder Cabinet
Committee.
